50104659.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to TPH-1 (unknown origin) by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Binding Affinity of Compound 9a with Tph-1. All experiments were carried out on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare, Uppsala, Sweden) at 15 °C. Tph-1 was covalently immobilized on parallel channels of a CM5 sensor chip according to the manufacturer’s protocol. The sensor chip surface was activated by a 5 min injection of 0.4 M N-ethyl-N’-(3-(dimethylamino)propyl) carbodiimide and 0.1 M N-hydroxysuccinimide. The compound 9a was serially diluted in the running buffer AMF (containing 10 mM Heps (pH 7.4), 3 mM EDTA, 150 mM NaCl, 0.005% Surfactant P20, 10 μM GDP, 4 mM MgCl2, 1 mM dithiothreitol, 10 mM NaF, 10 mM MgCl2) supplemented with 0.1% DMSO. The solution of 9a was injected for 40 s at the flow rate of 5.0 μL/min, and the dissociation was allowed for 90 s at 15 °C. Furthermore, buffer blanks were used as the positive control and double referencing. All data were corrected for nonspecific binding and Global fitting using the BIA-evaluation program. The experiments were performed more than three times.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Figure 2. SPR analysis of the binding of compound 9a to Tph-1. Sensorgrams were obtained by injecting five different concentrations in running buffer: 50.00, 12.50, 6.25, 3.12, and 1.56 μM at the flow rate of 30 μL/min. The concentration of Tph-1 was approximately 5.00 μM. RU: resonance units.
original_paragraph.Results section: The results revealed that 9a efficiently interacted with the immobilized Tph-1 and demonstrated a concentration dependent response (Figure 2) and a clearly discernible exponential curve during both the association and dissociation phases (Supporting Information Figure 3). The sensorgram obtained for the 9a interacting with Tph-1 was fitted to a single-site biomolecular interaction model (A + B = AB) with rapid association rates and rapid dissociation rates.
